discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single spins in solids (nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond), founding solid-state quantum sensing

nominees.name: Jörg Wrachtrup
nominees.affiliation: University of Stuttgart and Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Germany

subfield: Quantum physics / condensed matter (solid-state spin qubits and quantum sensing)
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko achieved optically detected magnetic resonance and coherent control of a single electron spin in a solid, the nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, and showed quantum gates between single electron and nuclear spins at room temperature. Lukin, with Wrachtrup and others, showed that such a single spin acts as an atomic-scale magnetometer with nanoscale resolution under ambient conditions. Together these discoveries turned a fragile quantum property of one defect into a measurable, controllable resource. They created a new field: quantum sensing with solid-state spins, now used to image magnetism in materials, currents in devices, and signals in living cells, including nanoscale NMR. They also laid the foundation for spin-photon interfaces and quantum-network nodes. This work launched a broad family of defect qubits in diamond, silicon carbide and other hosts, and spurred a worldwide research and industrial effort.
